_about: Public bug-bounty and vulnerability disclosure platforms whose program scopes Amass reads. A program's in-scope list is the organization declaring assets it is responsible for, so once a program is tied to an organization by first-party evidence the listed assets are strong, review-only ownership evidence (signals.json bug-bounty-scope, for both its uses). Each platform has a key (the prefix of the program Account's unique_id, <key>:<handle>), a title, the keyless feed that publishes every public program with its scope (feed, a JSON array of programs), the fields of a program record that name its handle in priority order (handle_fields; when company_field is set the handle is <company>/<handle>), the template of a program page when the record gives none (page, placeholder {handle}), the hosts program pages live on (hosts, which a security.txt link must point to for the link to tie a program to an organization), the DNS TXT record prefix the platform has customers publish to verify a domain (txt_prefix, optional; such a record on a domain a program lists ties the program to the domain's owner), and documentation of the feed in source. The feeds are a community mirror updated many times a day; Amass downloads each at most once a day and keeps it on disk.
